key_insight: A discrete differential geometry phase-field model can capture fracture and large post-failure deformation in thin, highly flexible structures on the same evolving midsurface.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers predict cracking, tearing, snap-through, and reconfiguration in flexible thin devices such as stretchable electronics and soft structural components.
method: Phase field is defined directly on a triangulated midsurface and coupled to discrete membrane and bending energies.
A staggered solve with an active-set constraint enforces crack irreversibility.
A degradation-deletion step removes nearly failed elements and reconstructs topology to allow full crack opening and large reconfiguration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite element results for 2D fracture and successful reproduction of 3D tearing experiments, including crack convergence and coalescence.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion and topology reconstruction steps may be sensitive to mesh resolution and numerical thresholds near crack tips.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
